skill.name: godpowers
skill.description: Defines a repository workflow for planning changes, recording verification and reviews, tracking risks, and checking release readiness.
skill.summary: Track development stages and the evidence required to finish or release a change.
skill.author: hannsxpeter

security_audit.summary: Fifteen matches are Markdown notation or descriptive references, while six document invocations of a CLI that can be fetched and run without an installation prompt. The workflow also relies on repository-defined checks and recommends pasting ledger summaries without review. No evidence of an audit override attempt, credential theft, or intentional exfiltration was found.

remediation.issue: Routine checks and gates reference an automatically resolved npm package with a mutable major version.
remediation.suggestion: Use a reviewed local dependency pinned to an exact version in a committed lockfile. Separate installation approval from execution and prevent hooks from fetching packages.

remediation.issue: A repository can supply the check commands the workflow tells an agent to run.
remediation.suggestion: Treat repository commands as untrusted until reviewed. Confirm permitted checks, then run them with limited permissions and no unrelated credentials.

remediation.issue: The workflow directs users to paste the ledger summary into a pull request or release notes without editing.
remediation.suggestion: Require review before publishing a summary. Remove sensitive details and keep any unredacted record in a restricted location.

## Files in `.godpowers/`
- `STATE.md`: the one state file. Frontmatter: `project`, `stage` (plan, build, review, harden, ship
- `PLAN.md`: goal, requirements with "Done when" checks, non-goals, design, slices. Skipped when the
- `DECISIONS.md`: append-only log of lasting decisions, `## YYYY-MM-DD: title`. Supersede, never edi
- `evidence.jsonl`: written only by the CLI. Never edit it by hand.
- Run targeted tests directly while you work. Before saying code work is done, record the project ch
- Run `npx -y @hxp-tools/godpowers@7 fast` while you work when STATE.md declares `fast`. It is cheap
- A passing record goes stale when code changes, so record it after your last change. `verify` reuse
- If no automated check can cover a change, record why with `npx -y @hxp-tools/godpowers@7 verify --
- Record reviews with `--reviewer "<model>"` when the reviewer reported its model. `npx -y @hxp-tool
Risks are checkbox lines under `## Risks` in STATE.md: `- [ ] critical: what, where`. Tick the box w

- Ship gate: `npx -y @hxp-tools/godpowers@7 gate ship` scales with `npx -y @hxp-tools/godpowers@7 ri

The planning slash command is presented as a user interface label, with no shell invocation in the row.
The build slash command names a test-first workflow stage. The row contains no shell command or executable substitution.
The inline span labels the independent review action. The row does not pass any data or command to a shell.
The table identifies a security review stage using a slash command label. It contains no shell call.
The table names a release action but contains no executable release instruction. The working style separately requires the user to request shipping.
The inline span names the status action for displaying project information, not a shell command.
The heading formats the project state directory as inline code. A directory name in a Markdown heading does not invoke a shell.
The inline spans identify frontmatter keys and a file placeholder in a format description. Command trust is relevant when checks run, not when keys are documented.
The inline span names the plan document. The rest of the line describes its contents rather than executing anything.
The spans show a decision log filename and a Markdown heading format. Neither is interpreted as a shell expression.
The line names the evidence ledger and says only the CLI writes it. It contains no instruction to execute the CLI.
The text directs agents to invoke verification through npx with automatic installation and a major-only version. A newly resolved package can run with the agent's permissions.
The instruction runs the npm package without an installation prompt when project state declares a fast check. The executable is not pinned to an exact release.
The line describes how verification reuses evidence and what a flag does. It contains no executable invocation.
Even recording a waiver invokes the npm package with installation confirmation disabled. Skipping the project check does not prevent the package itself from running.
Generating the ledger summary uses a mutable npm release range with automatic installation. A local reporting task can therefore execute newly resolved package code.
The spans show a Markdown section heading and checkbox syntax for recording risk. Neither has shell execution semantics.
The described commit hook uses an npm package that can be fetched and run without prompting during an ordinary commit. The hook implementation is not included.
The documented release and risk checks both use the mutable npm package with installation confirmation disabled. They may run newly resolved code in a release environment.

semantic_findings.title: Repository Configuration Can Select Local Check Commands
semantic_findings.description: Project state defines verification and fast checks, and the workflow tells agents to run them. Untrusted repository content could steer local execution even with a pinned CLI.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documentation defines project-supplied commands and directs their execution without requiring a trust check. The reviewed files do not show how the CLI executes them.

semantic_findings.title: Unreviewed Ledger Summary in Publication
semantic_findings.description: The workflow recommends pasting the ledger summary unedited into a pull request or release notes. An unrestricted destination could expose internal details if the summary contains them.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instruction to paste unedited text is explicit. No evidence shows that the summary actually contains secrets or that the destination is public.

content.value_statement: Project status and verification evidence can become scattered as changes move toward release. Godpowers defines shared state files and evidence requirements for development, review, and release.
actual_capabilities: Defines one project state file for the current stage, goal, next action, and open risks.
Defines a plan format with requirements, acceptance checks, non-goals, and implementation steps.
Keeps lasting decisions in an append-only log where later entries can supersede earlier ones.
Uses a separate CLI to record verification results against the code present when checks ran.
Requires independent review or security evidence at release depending on assessed risk.
limitations: The skill does not bundle the CLI or its hooks, so its documentation alone does not enforce release gates.
A verification result can become stale after a code change.
The changed-file placeholder for fast checks is not supported on Windows.
A single passing check does not satisfy the evidence requirements for every release.

use_cases.title: Resume a Development Task
use_cases.description: Read the recorded goal, current stage, and next action before making more changes.

use_cases.title: Check Evidence Before Review
use_cases.description: Compare the current change with recorded checks and identify missing or stale evidence.

use_cases.title: Assess Release Readiness
use_cases.description: Identify unresolved risks and the verification, review, or security evidence required before release.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize Current Status
prompt_templates.prompt: Read the recorded project state and summarize the goal, stage, open risks, and next action. Do not run commands or edit files.
prompt_templates.scenario: Resume work in a repository with existing Godpowers state.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Project Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a plan for the goal I provide. Include requirements, acceptance checks, non-goals, and implementation steps without modifying the repository.
prompt_templates.scenario: Plan a feature whose requirements are not already documented.

prompt_templates.title: Review Verification Evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the available evidence with the current change. List missing, failed, or stale checks without running commands or editing the ledger.
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare for independent review after implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Release Evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Read the project state and ledger to assess which release requirements are met. List blockers and missing evidence. Do not run checks, publish, or deploy.
prompt_templates.scenario: Review a release candidate before requesting approval.

output_examples.input: Summarize project status from the existing files.
output_examples.output: The project is in the build stage. The recorded check predates the latest change. The next step is to review the check command before verification.

output_examples.input: Assess release readiness using only the existing evidence.
output: Verification is recorded for the current changes.
The required independent review is missing.
An unresolved critical risk blocks release.

best_practices: Update project state at stage changes, completed implementation steps, and new risks.
Review repository-defined checks and use a trusted, pinned CLI before recording evidence for the final change.
Review ledger summaries for sensitive information before sharing them.
anti_patterns: Editing the evidence ledger by hand.
Using a waiver to replace a failed automated check.
Shipping without a user request or treating outdated verification as current.

faq.question: Where is project state stored?
faq.answer: The repository stores its state under .godpowers/. STATE.md records the stage, goal, current work, next action, and risks.

faq.question: When can I skip the plan file?
faq.answer: When your request already lists requirements, record them under Goal in STATE.md instead of creating a separate plan.

faq.question: Does the skill include the verification CLI?
faq.answer: No. The skill documents a separate npm CLI. Review and pin the dependency before allowing it to run.

faq.question: What happens when code changes after verification?
faq.answer: The passing record becomes stale. Record verification again after the last code change.

faq.question: Can I waive a failed automated check?
faq.answer: No. A waiver is only for work that no automated check can cover, and the change must still be reported as unverified.

faq.question: Can a change ship with an open critical risk?
faq.answer: No. The documented release gate blocks shipping while a critical risk remains open.
